title: Understanding the Model
text: Let's start by breaking down Tina's model: \( \hat{y}=2\theta_0+\theta_0**{4}\theta_1x-e**{2\theta_1}x**{2} \). Notice how each term involves \( $$\theta_0$$ \) and \( $$\theta_1$$ \). Think about how changes in these parameters affect the model's output.

title: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
text: The Mean Squared Error is calculated as \( L=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\hat{y_i})**2 \). Consider how \( \hat{y} \) is defined in Tina's model and how it affects the MSE.

title: Gradient Vector
text: The gradient vector \( \frac{\partial{L}}{\partial{\theta}} \) involves partial derivatives of the loss function with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \) and \( $$\theta_1$$ \). Focus on how each term in \( \hat{y} \) contributes to these derivatives.

title: Partial Derivative with Respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \)
text: Consider the term \( 2\theta_0 \) in \( \hat{y} \). What is the partial derivative of \( L \) with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \)?

title: Partial Derivative with Respect to \( $$\theta_1$$ \)
text: Now, consider the term \( \theta_0**{4}\theta_1x \) in \( \hat{y} \). What is the partial derivative of \( L \) with respect to \( $$\theta_1$$ \)?
